newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto to buy Holden's, seed distributors.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto to buy Holden's, seed distributors.

text.p: Monsanto Co. said Monday it agreed to pay up to $1.02 billion to acquire three companies involved in hybrid seed production.

It said it was buying Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc., a producer of germplasm and inbreds -- or parent seeds -- used by retail seed companies to create hybrid seeds, as well as Corn States Hybrid Service Inc. and Corn States International, the exclusive worldwide marketing and sales representatives for Holden's products.
More than 35 percent of the corn acres planted in the United States use genetic material developed by Holden's, Monsanto said.
Corn States and Corn States International, with operations in the United States, Europe and South America, provide Holden's germplasm and specialised services to seed companies worldwide.

"Holden's germplasm is an important building block. It will provide an excellent delivery mechanism for our biotechnology innovations in corn," Monsanto Chairman Robert Shapiro said in a statement announcing the deal.
Monsanto said Holden's, Corn States and Corn States International will be run as independent units within the company. Holden's will remain in Williamsburg, Iowa, and Corn States in Des Moines, Iowa.

"The employees of Holden's and Corn States are important to our long-term success," Shapiro said. "We value their knowledge and experience in plant breeding and seed production, their strong relationships in the marketplace and their commitment to their customers and the world of agriculture."
He added that Holden's President Ron Holden will lead the business and provide counsel to Monsanto's broad agricultural operations.

Monsanto, among other agricultural companies, has developed genetically enhanced crops by implanting genes to deliver specific traits. Those traits include the ability to fight off certain insects and tolerance to certain herbicides.
Monsanto said the transaction will be completed as soon as possible, subject to government approvals and other terms.

Monsanto said Holden's corn breed expertise and Corn States' array of services to seed companies will play important roles in increasing the value of Monsanto's other crop development programmes, including those involving soybeans, wheat, cotton and rice.

On Dec. 23, 1996, Monsanto's YieldGard corn, which is genetically protected against the European corn borer, was given final U.S. regulatory approval. Other products in development include Roundup Ready corn, which can withstand Monsanto's Roundup herbicide, and corn that is genetically protected against corn rootworm.

Analysts said last week that Monsanto was expected to purchase Holden's, which would help in its development of biotech crops. The purchase also would be a defensive measure to keep competitors from gaining Holden's.

Monsanto said the acquisitions are an important piece of its strategy. It is in the process of creating a new life sciences company that will combine its existing agricultural, food and pharmaceutical businesses. It also seeks to develop new businesses that have synergies with these fields.
Monsanto previously said it would spin off its chemical businesses.
Monsanto's stock gained 87.5 cents to $40.50 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
